key_insight: An expert-grounded causal AI model suggested personalized early fluid and vasopressor dosing for septic shock in the ICU, with treatment effects varying by baseline physiology.
clinical_relevance: The approach could help standardize early haemodynamic resuscitation while accounting for patient heterogeneity, but it is not yet proven to improve outcomes in practice.
method: Built a graphical causal inference model from clinician knowledge to estimate heterogeneous treatment effects.
Trained on 1,706 MIMIC ICU admissions and externally validated on 1,450 eICU admissions.
Focused on the first 6 hours after ICU admission, comparing fluid and vasopressor dose deviations with survival and clinical improvement.
evidence_signal: External validation showed AUROCs of 0.72 for survival and 0.70 for clinical improvement, with performance comparable to predictive baselines.
watch_item: The recommendations remain observational and confounded by indication, so prospective evaluation is still needed before clinical implementation.
paper_title: The Causal Artificial Intelligence Clinician for early haemodynamic management of septic shock in ICU
